papers.title: Integrating heterogeneity into topologically associating domain boundary prediction in large genomic context in human.
papers.abstract: A fundamental understanding of genome organization relies on accurately annotating topologically associating domains (TADs) and their boundaries. This is crucial for understanding how cis-regulatory elements regulate gene expression. To go beyond calling TADs and boundaries from Hi-C data, several machine learning-based methods have been proposed to go the step further and predict TAD boundaries from genomic sequences. As the growing evidence of TADs and their boundaries, TADs have been proved exhibiting diverse properties, such as differences in replication timing and epigenetic patterns. How
papers.summary: This paper presents a new machine learning approach that improves prediction of topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries from genomic sequences by explicitly incorporating heterogeneity across TADs and using large genomic context. The method outperforms existing predictors, highlighting the importance of accounting for diverse TAD properties in sequence-based boundary prediction.

papers.title: Research priorities in chronic lung allograft dysfunction: A machine learning-assisted bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), the leading cause of death beyond year one post-transplant, encompasses bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS), restrictive allograft syndrome (RAS), and mixed allograft syndrome (MAS), formalized by the 2019 ISHLT consensus. How thematic priorities have evolved and whether research effort tracks phenotype burden have not been systematically examined.
papers.summary: This study uses a machine learning-assisted bibliometric analysis to map research priorities in chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), a major cause of death after lung transplantation. It examines how thematic focus has evolved and whether research output aligns with the clinical burden of CLAD phenotypes, such as bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome and restrictive allograft syndrome.

papers.title: Identification of IL1RN, MUC1, and SERPINA1 as key NET-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis-associated intestinal fibrosis via bioinformatics and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Long-term recurrent episodes of ulcerative colitis (UC) can lead to intestinal fibrosis (IF), which severely affects patient prognosis. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been identified as critical drivers of various fibrotic diseases; however, their precise role and regulatory mechanisms in UC-associated intestinal fibrosis (UC-IF) remain to be systematically elucidated. Therefore, identifying the key regulatory genes through which NETs participate in UC-IF is highly important for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.
papers.summary: This study identifies IL1RN, MUC1, and SERPINA1 as key neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis-associated intestinal fibrosis using bioinformatics and experimental validation. These findings may aid in the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

papers.title: Transformers for molecular property prediction: domain adaptation efficiently improves performance.
papers.abstract: Over the past six years, molecular transformer models have become a part of the computational toolbox for drug discovery. Most existing models are pre-trained on millions to billions of molecules from large-scale unlabeled datasets such as ZINC or ChEMBL. However, the extent to which such large-scale pre-training improves molecular property prediction remains unclear. This study investigates the potential of transformer models for molecular property prediction while addressing their current limitations. We explore strategies to enhance performance, including the influence of pre-training datas
papers.summary: This study evaluates transformer models for molecular property prediction and finds that domain adaptation—fine-tuning on task-relevant data—significantly improves performance over generic large-scale pre-training. The work clarifies the conditions under which pre-training helps and offers practical guidance for applying transformers in drug discovery.

papers.title: Early Detection Methods for Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Clinical Screening to Multimodal AI.
papers.abstract: Early detection of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in young children is essential for timely referral, developmental monitoring, and access to early intervention. However, conventional screening and diagnostic pathways often depend on parent-report instruments, episodic clinical observation, and specialist-administered assessments, which may delay identification during the first years of life. This scoping review maps the methodological landscape of early ASD detection from traditional clinical screening to multimodal artificial intelligence (AI). A structured literature search was conducted ac
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the methodological landscape of early autism spectrum disorder (ASD) detection, from traditional clinical screening tools to emerging multimodal artificial intelligence approaches. It highlights the limitations of conventional parent-report and specialist-based methods and discusses how AI could enable earlier, more objective identification during the critical first years of life.

papers.title: Dynamic Quality Prediction and Intelligent Classification of Litopenaeus vannamei in Cold Chain Based on Tad-Transformer.
papers.abstract: Temperature fluctuations in cold chain logistics accelerate protein degradation, lipid oxidation, and color deterioration of Litopenaeus vannamei, reducing product value and compromising food safety. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic quality prediction method based on the Tad-Transformer neural network. First, storage experiments were conducted under six cold chain temperature conditions to collect multi-dimensional physicochemical and texture data. Core quality indicators were selected through temperature sensitivity analysis, and a time-series dataset was constructed. Seco
papers.summary: This paper presents a Tad-Transformer neural network model for dynamic quality prediction of Litopenaeus vannamei (whiteleg shrimp) during cold chain logistics, using multi-dimensional physicochemical and texture data collected under six temperature conditions. The model enables intelligent classification of shrimp quality, helping to reduce food safety risks and economic losses from temperature fluctuations.

papers.title: EMMA-STRAT: a multi-omics based machine learning framework for stratification of endometrial carcinoma molecular subtypes and MSI status.
papers.abstract: Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy, with molecular heterogeneity influencing prognosis and treatment response. Although TCGA-defined molecular subtypes and multi-omics datasets have improved biological understanding of UCEC, externally evaluated computational frameworks for molecular stratification remain limited. To address this, we developed EMMA-STRAT, a supervised multi-omics machine learning framework integrating mRNA expression, miRNA expression, and DNA methylation data to classify UCEC genomic subtypes and microsatellite instability (M
papers.summary: EMMA-STRAT is a new machine learning framework that integrates mRNA, miRNA, and DNA methylation data to classify endometrial cancer molecular subtypes and microsatellite instability status. It addresses the lack of externally validated computational tools for molecular stratification of this cancer type, potentially improving prognosis and treatment decisions.

papers.title: Omics Data Discovery Agents: Agent-Supported Retrieval, Reanalysis, and Synthesis of Published Omics Data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g. protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs larg
papers.summary: This paper introduces an agentic framework that uses large language model-based agents to automatically retrieve, reanalyze, and synthesize published omics data from the literature and public repositories. The system addresses the challenge of scattered and inconsistently formatted data by automating the discovery and integration of raw and intermediate data files, making them more accessible for computational reuse.

papers.title: The Continuity Trap in Data Science Health Research.
papers.abstract: Secondary use is now the ordinary condition of data science health research rather than an exception to it. Electronic health records collected for clinical care become prediction tools and inputs for generative AI; imaging archives become foundation-model corpora; genomic datasets become resources for polygenic risk scores; and legacy biospecimens become renewable, indefinitely distributable cell lines. Governance has responded by emphasizing verifiable instruments such as provenance logs, repository approvals, broad-consent forms, data-use agreements, model cards, records of processing, and
papers.summary: This paper argues that secondary use of health data is now the norm in data science research, not an exception, and that current governance tools (like consent forms and data-use agreements) are insufficient to address the ethical and practical challenges this creates. It introduces the concept of a 'continuity trap' to describe the mismatch between the static, one-time nature of these governance instruments and the dynamic, ongoing reuse of data across multiple contexts.

papers.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of Synthetic Microbiota for Next-Generation Immunomodulatory Applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota aimed at immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current classical machine learning and shallow deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and enforcing biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for advanced computational approaches to design effective microbiome-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Post-translational Modification Site Prediction: Progress and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are pivotal in modulating protein function and cellular processes. However, experimental identification of PTM sites remains costly and labor-intensive. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled accurate and scalable in silico PTM site prediction from large-scale proteomic data. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of AI-driven PTM site prediction across more than ten PTM classes, covering single-PTM site prediction, multiple-PTM site prediction, inter-site crosstalk prediction, and functional prediction o
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of AI-driven methods for predicting post-translational modification (PTM) sites, covering more than ten PTM classes and tasks including single- and multiple-PTM prediction, inter-site crosstalk, and functional prediction. It highlights recent advances in using artificial intelligence to enable accurate and scalable in silico prediction from large-scale proteomic data, addressing the high cost and labor of experimental identification.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell transcriptomics and genomic mutation analysis identifies an immunotherapy-resistant tumor subcluster and validates ARNTL2 as a malignant driver in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a critical clinical challenge, and the mechanisms underlying resistance-associated intratumoral heterogeneity are poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with genomic mutation analysis in lung adenocarcinoma to identify a tumor subcluster associated with immunotherapy resistance, and validates ARNTL2 as a key malignant driver in this context. The findings provide new insights into resistance mechanisms and highlight ARNTL2 as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a CDH3-Associated Malignant Epithelial State and Immunosuppressive Niche to Predict Prognosis in Thymic Epithelial Tumors.
papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies whose aggressive epithelial states and microenvironmental organization remain poorly defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, bulk transcriptomics, functional assays, xenograft validation, and computational pathology to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in TETs. We identified a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state located at the origin of malignant-state trajectories and enriched for stem-like and EMT-related features. Spatial transc
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and other approaches to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in thymic epithelial tumors (TETs). The authors identify a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state with stem-like and EMT features that predicts prognosis and is linked to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, offering potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial decoupling of plaque and circulating immune programs defines a robust gene signature in atherosclerosis: A multi-cohort integrative analysis.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is driven by chronic vascular inflammation, yet the relationship between immune activity within atherosclerotic lesions and systemic immune signals in peripheral blood remains poorly defined. In this study, we performed an integrative multi-cohort analysis of gene expression profiles from atherosclerotic tissues, peripheral blood, and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to characterize spatial immune heterogeneity in AS. Differential expression and enrichment analyses revealed divergent immune-related transcriptional patterns between plaques and blood, indicating a dissoci
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-cohort gene expression and single-cell data from atherosclerotic plaques and peripheral blood to reveal that immune-related transcriptional programs are spatially decoupled between the two compartments. The authors identify a robust gene signature that captures this dissociation, which may improve understanding of atherosclerosis as a systemic versus local inflammatory disease.

papers.title: Structure-based TCR-pMHC binding prediction and generalization to unseen peptides.
papers.abstract: The interaction between T-cell receptors (TCRs) with the peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (MHC) intricately impacts the functional specificity of T-cell-mediated adaptive immune response. Consequently, implication in immunotherapy has contributed to the ever-growing computational methods for TCR recognition, which have recently attracted structure-based approaches due to advancements in protein structure modeling. Despite access to structural information of the predicted binding interface, graph neural network (GNN)-based TCR-pMHC binding specificity classifiers tend to show poor
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based approach for predicting TCR-pMHC binding specificity, leveraging predicted structural information of the binding interface. The authors address the challenge of generalizing to unseen peptides, which is critical for immunotherapy applications. Their method likely improves upon existing GNN-based classifiers by better utilizing structural features.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Liver Transplantation: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a transformative paradigm within transplantation medicine, offering advanced computational approaches capable of integrating heterogeneous clinical, biological, imaging, and molecular datasets to improve predictive accuracy and decision-making. Liver transplantation represents a uniquely complex clinical domain characterized by high-dimensional data, nonlinear interactions among risk factors, and critical time-dependent decision processes, thereby providing an ideal context for AI-enabled analytics.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines the application of artificial intelligence in liver transplantation, highlighting its potential to integrate diverse clinical, biological, imaging, and molecular data for improved predictive accuracy and decision-making in this complex medical field.

papers.title: Hierarchical Discrete Representations for Coarse-to-Fine Protein Conformation Generation.
papers.abstract: Protein conformation generation remains a fundamental challenge in structural biology and machine learning. Proteins are highly dynamic macromolecules, and their functions are governed not only by static 3D structures but also by their conformational flexibility. Therefore, generating a diverse ensemble of physically plausible structures is crucial for modeling conformational heterogeneity, characterizing intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), and supporting structure-based drug discovery. However, existing generative models often operate in continuous coordinate space. This approach makes
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical discrete representation approach for protein conformation generation, enabling coarse-to-fine modeling of structural ensembles. The method addresses limitations of continuous coordinate-space generative models by capturing conformational flexibility and diversity, which is important for studying intrinsically disordered proteins and drug discovery.

papers.title: Structure-aware deep learning enhances m6A prediction and reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures.
papers.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant mRNA modification in eukaryotes, plays essential roles in gene regulation and disease pathogenesis. Computational prediction of m6A sites offers a scalable alternative to costly experimental approaches, yet current methods rely predominantly on linear sequence features. This overlooks potentially informative RNA structural context, which is associated with local methylation patterns and may provide complementary predictive information beyond linear sequence motifs. To incorporate this complementary information, we propose SMART-m6A (Sequence-structur
papers.summary: This paper introduces SMART-m6A, a deep learning method that integrates RNA structural information with sequence data to improve prediction of m6A modification sites. The approach reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures, demonstrating that structural context provides complementary predictive power beyond linear sequence motifs.

papers.title: Computationally Evidence-Grounded Sequence-First Design of Peptide Binders.
papers.abstract: Peptide binders provide a versatile modality for modulating protein targets that are poorly addressed by small molecules, but their discovery is constrained by sample-intensive screening or reliance on structural templates. Sequence-first generation offers a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable or representative structures, yet existing approaches often sacrifice target-specific control for diversity and are further limited by the imperfect transfer of protein language-model priors to short peptides. Here, we report BOND-PEP, an evidence-grounded framework for sequence-only peptide
papers.summary: The paper introduces BOND-PEP, a computational framework for designing peptide binders using only sequence information, without requiring structural templates. It addresses limitations of existing sequence-first methods by improving target-specific control and adapting protein language models to short peptides, offering a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable structures.

papers.title: From Multi-Omics to Mechanism: Nucleocapsid-RCHY1-JUNB Axis Underlies SARS-CoV-2 Related Atrial Fibrillation Vulnerability.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 exposure has been linked to cardiovascular complications, including atrial fibrillation (AF), but the host pathways coupling viral factors to atrial remodeling and AF vulnerability remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
papers.summary: This study investigates how SARS-CoV-2 infection contributes to atrial fibrillation by identifying a molecular axis involving the viral nucleocapsid protein, the host E3 ligase RCHY1, and the transcription factor JUNB. Using multi-omics approaches, the authors show that this axis drives atrial remodeling and increases AF vulnerability, providing a mechanistic link between viral exposure and cardiac arrhythmia.

papers.title: Peptide language pragmatic analysis and two-stage hierarchical learning framework for therapeutic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides exert pivotal effects in diverse biological processes, and have attracted significant interest in the field of biomedicine in recent years. However, most existing methods often fail to adequately capture the intricate interactions among amino acid residues and the contextual dependencies within peptide sequences, which hampers the extraction of deep semantic representations and ultimately restricts predictive performance. Moreover, the task of multi-functional therapeutic peptide prediction is inherently constrained by the challenge of imbalanced multi-label classification
papers.summary: This paper introduces a two-stage hierarchical learning framework with peptide language pragmatic analysis to improve therapeutic peptide prediction. The method better captures amino acid interactions and contextual dependencies, addressing limitations of existing approaches and tackling imbalanced multi-label classification for multi-functional peptides.

papers.title: Exploring dual-use risks of large language models for new psychoactive substances: a severity-based vulnerability analysis.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have profoundly transformed scientific research in chemistry, enabling literature mining, the prediction of physicochemical and biological properties, and even the generation of novel molecular structures. However, such tools also raise concerns regarding malicious use, particularly in the context of the clandestine synthesis of new psychoactive substances (NPSs). In this study, we evaluate simulated scenarios of interaction with LLM-based chatbots to explore potential vulnerabilities in the provision of information that could facilitate illicit
papers.journal: The International journal on drug policy
papers.summary: This study evaluates the dual-use risks of large language models (LLMs) in the context of new psychoactive substances (NPSs), simulating interactions to identify vulnerabilities where LLMs might provide information that could facilitate illicit synthesis. The authors propose a severity-based vulnerability analysis to assess and mitigate these risks, highlighting the need for safeguards in chemistry-focused AI tools.

papers.title: Generalizable cancer detection from ultra-low-pass WGS via deep contextual modeling of cfDNA sequences.
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing (ULP-WGS) of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a cost-efficient strategy for cancer detection, but its clinical application is limited by extreme data sparsity and poor model generalization. We developed Fragmentia-AI™ WGS, a mutation-calling-independent framework that uses a transformer-based multiple-instance learning architecture with sequential fine-tuning across tumor fraction (TF) strata to extract latent cancer-associated signals from ULP-WGS data. Model performance was evaluated in multiple independent cohorts, including a pan-cancer test set covering
papers.summary: This paper introduces Fragmentia-AI™ WGS, a transformer-based deep learning framework that detects cancer from ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing of cell-free DNA without relying on mutation calling. The model uses multiple-instance learning and sequential fine-tuning across tumor fraction strata to extract latent cancer signals, achieving generalizable performance across multiple independent pan-cancer cohorts despite extreme data sparsity.

papers.title: Using the DNA language model, GROVER, to parse effects of sequence, chromatin and regulatory features on genome stability.
papers.abstract: Genome stability is shaped by DNA sequence and chromatin context, but their relative contributions to double-strand break (DSB) sensitivity remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses GROVER, a DNA language model, to analyze how DNA sequence, chromatin, and regulatory features contribute to genome stability, specifically double-strand break (DSB) sensitivity. The findings help disentangle the relative roles of these factors in determining where breaks occur.

papers.title: Contrastive learning unites sequence and structure in a global representation of protein space.
papers.abstract: Establishing a coherent mapping of the relationships among all known proteins is crucial for elucidating processes of protein emergence and evolution. Yet the capacity to fully capture relationships of protein similarity is complicated by the nonstraightforward interplay between sequence and structure; indeed, proteins with unrelated sequences can adopt similar structures, and, conversely, proteins with similar or identical sequences can manifest radically different structures. Here, we introduce Contrastive Learning Sequence-Structure (CLSS), a contrastive protein language model (PLM) trained
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This paper introduces CLSS, a contrastive protein language model that jointly learns from both sequence and structure data to create a unified representation of protein space. By aligning sequence and structure embeddings, CLSS captures relationships that are missed by sequence-only or structure-only models, potentially improving our understanding of protein evolution and function.

papers.title: DeepPNI: a language- and graph-based model for mutation-driven protein-nucleic acid binding energetics.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions (PNIs) are central to fundamental biological processes, and mutations can disrupt these interactions by altering local structural features and binding free energy. Here, we present DeepPNI, a deep learning regression model that integrates sequence- and structure-based features to estimate mutation-induced changes in binding free energy in protein-nucleic acid complexes. The model was developed using a comprehensive dataset of 1754 mutations spanning protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes, representing one of the largest curated datasets for PNI binding free ene
papers.summary: DeepPNI is a new deep learning model that predicts how mutations affect the binding strength of protein-nucleic acid interactions. It combines sequence and structural features and was trained on a large dataset of 1,754 mutations, making it a valuable tool for understanding the impact of genetic variants on these essential biological processes.

papers.title: DNAreader: accurate prediction of DNA-binding residues in structured and disordered proteins using transformers and contrastive learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate predictions of DNA-binding residues (DBRs) in protein sequences facilitate decoding molecular-level mechanisms underlying cellular functions that involve protein-DNA interactions. While dozens of these predictors have been released, they target either structured or intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and the latter were trained to predict less detailed DNA-binding IDRs rather than DBRs. Given this dichotomy, the structure-trained methods underperform on disordered proteins, and vice versa. Moreover, they suffer from high cross-prediction rates, incorrectly labeling many residues
papers.summary: DNAreader is a new deep learning tool that accurately predicts DNA-binding residues in both structured and disordered protein regions, overcoming a key limitation of existing predictors that specialize in only one type. It uses transformers and contrastive learning to reduce false positives and improve accuracy across diverse protein types.

papers.title: Exploring the mechanism underlying negative pressure wound therapy in promoting the healing of diabetic foot ulcers via integrated multi-omics and bioinformatics approaches.
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are one of the most serious complications of diabetes, closely associated with high amputation rates, mortality, and healthcare burdens, and the clinical treatment research is still limited. Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT) is a treatment modality for DFU, but its specific mechanisms promoting wound healing remain largely unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated multi-omics and bioinformatics to investigate how negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) promotes healing in diabetic foot ulcers, identifying key molecular pathways and potential therapeutic targets. The findings provide mechanistic insights into NPWT's beneficial effects, which could inform improved clinical strategies for DFU management.

papers.title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants.
papers.abstract: Flowering plants (angiosperms) exhibit extraordinary species diversity, ∼200-fold variation in genome size, and relatively compact coding regions, presenting both a unique challenge and opportunity for DNA language models. Here, we introduce PlantCAD2, an extended-context, plant-specific DNA language model with single-nucleotide resolution, pre-trained on 65 angiosperm genomes, together with a series of public benchmarks for evaluation. Comprehensive zero-shot testing shows that PlantCAD2 (676 million parameters) efficiently captures evolutionary conservation, surpassing the 7-billion-paramete
papers.summary: PlantCAD2 is a new DNA foundation model pre-trained on 65 flowering plant genomes that captures evolutionary conservation and genome function at single-nucleotide resolution, outperforming much larger models in zero-shot tests. It provides a powerful new resource for interpreting plant genomes and understanding gene regulation across angiosperms.

papers.title: Fine-grained structural classification of biosynthetic gene cluster-encoded products.
papers.abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are responsible the biosynthesis of many natural products, including a multitude of effective therapeutics and their precursors. Advances in genomic data collection as well as computational techniques have made it possible to identify BGCs at scale. However, accurately determining the types of BGC-encoded products from genomic content remains elusive.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method for fine-grained structural classification of natural products encoded by biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), addressing the challenge of predicting product types from genomic data. The approach improves accuracy over existing tools, enabling more precise functional annotation of BGCs at scale.

papers.title: Integrated Analysis of SNPs and Structural Variations via High-depth Whole-genome Sequencing Reveals the Genetic Architecture and Optimizes Genomic Prediction in Chickens.
papers.abstract: The characterization of genetic architecture and the optimization of genomic prediction are pivotal for the genetic improvement of complex traits in poultry. In this study, we investigated the genetic basis of 15 growth and carcass traits in an F2 chicken population (n = 877) using high-depth whole-genome sequencing with an average coverage of 31.2 × . By implementing an ensemble strategy involving four independent callers, we identified 35,924 high-confidence structural variations (SVs), with deletions being the most prevalent type. Combining SNPs and SVs enhanced genomic heritability for 14
papers.summary: This study used high-depth whole-genome sequencing to identify structural variants (SVs) in an F2 chicken population and analyzed their contribution to the genetic architecture of growth and carcass traits. Combining SNPs and SVs improved genomic heritability estimates and genomic prediction accuracy for these traits, highlighting the value of including SVs in genetic improvement programs for poultry.

papers.title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
papers.abstract: Genomic and protein foundation models (GFMs and PFMs) have demonstrated strong performance in learning the language of DNA and proteins, but their use in large-scale sequence generation is limited by the latency of autoregressive decoding. Because every token triggers a forward pass of a large Transformer, whose inference is relatively slow, long-sequence generation quickly becomes costly.
papers.summary: This paper introduces speculative decoding to accelerate inference in genomic and protein foundation models, reducing the latency of autoregressive sequence generation. By using a smaller draft model to propose tokens that are then verified in parallel by the large model, the method speeds up generation without sacrificing accuracy, making large-scale sequence generation more practical.

papers.title: scKanFormer: A Transformer-KAN framework with biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is accurately and efficiently identifying the cell type of each cell. Cell type annotation for scRNA-seq data not only needs to overcome batch effects caused by various factors but also requires effective handling of large-scale scRNA-seq datasets. Although deep learning has achieved remarkable progress in cell type annotation tasks, it still exhibits limitations in interpretability and robustness against batch effects. To tackle these issues, we propose a supervised framework based on the Transformer architecture, named s
papers.summary: This paper introduces scKanFormer, a Transformer-based framework with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) and biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data. It aims to improve interpretability and robustness against batch effects compared to existing deep learning methods.

papers.title: Deep learning for optoacoustic imaging of reversibly switchable proteins: training and performance testing using simulated multispectral optoacoustic tomography images.
papers.abstract: Reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) are a promising candidate for sensitive and quantitative optoacoustic (OA) imaging of genetically modified cell populations, such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells used in cancer immunotherapy. Although detection of rsOAPs has been demonstrated using classical machine learning approaches, there is still a need for higher detection sensitivity and more accurate quantification.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning approach for detecting and quantifying reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) in multispectral optoacoustic tomography images, using simulated training data to improve sensitivity and accuracy over classical machine learning methods. The approach is aimed at enabling better imaging of genetically modified cell populations, such as CAR T-cells in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: GeneInsight: Condensing gene set knowledge via language models.
papers.abstract: Gene set analysis often returns extensive annotations from multiple sources, requiring manual effort to identify coherent biological themes. We developed GeneInsight, an AI-powered tool that automates this by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering semantically related terms using sentence embeddings, and generating thematic summaries via large language model prompting. This enables researchers to identify biological themes that may be obscured when annotation sources are examined separately.
papers.summary: GeneInsight is an AI-powered tool that automates the interpretation of gene set analysis results by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering related terms using sentence embeddings, and generating coherent thematic summaries with large language models. This helps researchers identify overarching biological themes that might be missed when examining annotation sources individually, reducing manual effort.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance in hereditary cancer.
papers.abstract: Variant interpretation remains a major bottleneck in clinical genomics, with variants of uncertain significance (VUS) representing a critical unresolved challenge due to insufficient evidence for definitive classification. Existing in silico tools exhibit variable and often inconsistent performance complicating clinical decision-making, particularly in the context of hereditary cancer genomics.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning framework designed to improve the predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in hereditary cancer genes. The framework aims to address the inconsistency of existing in silico tools by providing more reliable classifications to aid clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Boundary-aware and uncertainty-guided deep learning for multimodal magnetic resonance imaging segmentation of stroke lesions.
papers.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke is a major cerebrovascular disease, and accurate lesion segmentation is important for quantitative image analysis and subsequent clinical assessment. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging, including diffusion-weighted imaging, apparent diffusion coefficient maps, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, provides complementary information for lesion delineation. However, lesion appearance may vary across sequences, and blurred boundaries or small scattered lesions can make multimodal feature fusion unstable.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning method for segmenting stroke lesions in multimodal MRI that explicitly handles blurred boundaries and small scattered lesions. The approach uses boundary-aware and uncertainty-guided modules to improve the stability of multimodal feature fusion, leading to more accurate lesion delineation.

papers.title: A tissue microenvironment analogous to certain tumor microenvironments facilitates HIV persistence.
papers.abstract: The HIV reservoir that establishes early upon infection and persists in tissues remains the primary barrier to a functional cure. While progress has been made to study the reservoir in blood compartments and specific cell types, knowledge gaps remain on the tissue microenvironment that facilitates persistence. The development of a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics pipeline has enabled the localization of foci of viral infection in tissues, rare events that are challenging to sample. Prior studies leveraging the pipeline have characterized the viral microenvironment (VME) gene s
papers.summary: This paper describes a tissue microenvironment, analogous to certain tumor microenvironments, that facilitates HIV persistence. Using a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics pipeline, the authors localized rare foci of viral infection in tissues and characterized the viral microenvironment gene signatures. The findings highlight parallels between HIV reservoir niches and tumor microenvironments, offering new insights into why HIV persists despite antiretroviral therapy.

papers.title: Plasmid-resolved genomics and machine learning-assisted profiling reveal Enterobacter soli as an overlooked host of a bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmid.
papers.abstract: Plasmid-mediated carbapenem resistance is a major public health concern, yet the role of under-characterized Enterobacter species in carrying clinically important resistance plasmids remains insufficiently defined. In particular, plasmid-resolved genomic information on bla NDM-1-positive Enterobacter soli is scarce, and it remains unclear whether clinical E. soli can harbor conserved bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmids related to those circulating among other Enterobacterales hosts.
papers.summary: This study uses plasmid-resolved genomics and machine learning to characterize Enterobacter soli as a previously overlooked host of a bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmid, showing that clinical E. soli can carry conserved carbapenem resistance plasmids related to those in other Enterobacterales. The findings highlight the importance of under-characterized species in the spread of antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: TPT: a compact CNN-transformer encoder for efficient microbial small protein modeling.
papers.abstract: Microbial small proteins, encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs), play essential roles in antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, and signaling pathways. However, their short length and rapid evolutionary rate present significant challenges for computational modeling.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TPT, a compact CNN-transformer hybrid encoder designed to improve computational modeling of microbial small proteins, which are difficult to analyze due to their short length and rapid evolution. The model efficiently captures sequence features to support functional prediction and characterization of these proteins.

papers.title: Microstructure-informed stage characterization of wheat endosperm refinement during shear comminution.
papers.abstract: Structural evolution of wheat endosperm particles during comminution can markedly influence flour processing and digestibility. While previous studies have mainly focused on differences among grinding endpoints, stage-dependent refinement under shear-dominant conditions remains unclear. This study characterized the structural and functional evolution of wheat endosperm particles during shear-dominant comminution. Coarse wheat endosperm particles were collected after predefined shear durations during shear-dominant comminution and examined using scanning electron microscopy and confocal laser s
papers.summary: This study characterizes how wheat endosperm particles structurally evolve during shear-dominant comminution, revealing stage-dependent refinement patterns that could influence flour processing and digestibility. Using microscopy techniques, the authors identify distinct structural changes across grinding stages, moving beyond endpoint comparisons to understand the dynamic process.

papers.title: Ferroptosis-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Multi-Omics and Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is one of the primary factors leading to end-stage renal disease. Ferroptosis, as a mechanism-related form of programmed cell death, has garnered increasing attention in DKD research. This study aimed to identify and validate ferroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for DKD.
papers.summary: This study identifies and validates ferroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) using a multi-omics and multi-cohort approach. The findings highlight specific ferroptosis-related genes that could serve as diagnostic markers, potentially improving early detection and understanding of DKD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Multimodal AI in high-grade serous ovarian cancer: integrated prediction and clinical decision-making.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) accounting for the majority of deaths. It is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage, characterized by extensive peritoneal dissemination and high rates of recurrence, which contribute to persistently poor survival despite advances in cytoreductive surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, and targeted therapies such as PARP inhibitors. Clinical outcomes are highly variable, reflecting substantial inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity at the genomic, cellular, and microenvironmental lev
papers.summary: This review discusses the application of multimodal AI integrating genomic, imaging, and clinical data for improved prediction and clinical decision-making in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). It highlights how such approaches can address tumor heterogeneity and variability in outcomes, potentially enhancing diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection.

papers.title: UNKAI: A Protein Functional Identity Prediction Model Based on ESM-C Latent Representations and the Attention Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of genome sequencing technologies has led to the accumulation of a vast number of protein sequences in public databases. However, a substantial proportion of these proteins remain functionally uncharacterized. Concurrently, the expansion of protein sequence data has enabled the development of protein language models (pLMs). By distilling billions of years of evolutionary history into a latent representational space, these models have acquired an unprecedented capacity to predict both the tertiary structures and functions of proteins. In this study, we developed a deep lea
papers.summary: The paper presents UNKAI, a deep learning model that predicts protein functional identity using ESM-C latent representations and an attention mechanism. It leverages protein language models to address the challenge of functionally uncharacterized proteins, offering a new computational tool for functional annotation.

papers.title: Clinical risk factors and machine learning for venous thromboembolism in lung cancer: an exploratory single-center study.
papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) represents a common and severe comorbidity in lung cancer patients. This study aimed to characterize the clinical features and independent risk factors associated with VTE in these individuals, and to evaluate the complementary utility of machine learning approaches in enhancing VTE risk stratification.
papers.summary: This exploratory single-center study identified clinical risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in lung cancer patients and evaluated machine learning models for VTE risk stratification. The findings suggest that machine learning can complement traditional risk assessment, potentially improving the identification of high-risk patients.

papers.title: Development of adaptive activation functions with curvature and range modulation for abstract image feature learning in complex CNNs for cross-domain applications.
papers.abstract: Deep learning architectures comprise hierarchies in modern machine learning studies, and these are not only full of semantic depth; they are also structured systematically by a sequence of nonlinear transformations. In particular, in convolutional neural networks, the activation functions are the canonical nonlinear construction blocks that control the expressiveness of the model, gradient flow in the process of back-propagation, and hierarchical feature abstraction. The canonical activation functions, which are the rectified linear unit (ReLU), the sigmoid, and the hyperbolic tangent (tanh) h
papers.summary: This paper introduces adaptive activation functions with curvature and range modulation for convolutional neural networks, aimed at improving abstract image feature learning across different domains. The proposed functions enhance model expressiveness and gradient flow compared to standard activations like ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh, as demonstrated in cross-domain applications.

papers.title: From subjective assessment to data-driven diagnosis: the AI revolution in multimodal early detection of Sjögren's disease.
papers.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD), a chronic autoimmune disorder affecting exocrine glands, faces significant diagnostic challenges due to its highly heterogeneous symptoms, subjective interpretation of imaging findings, and reliance on invasive biopsies, often resulting in delayed diagnosis by 3-7 years. This review posits that the integration of diverse data streams-from medical imaging to molecular omics-is the pivotal key to overcoming diagnostic heterogeneity, and that AI serves as the indispensable engine to power this integration. We systematically synthesize evidence showing that deep learning m
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-powered integration of diverse data streams—from medical imaging to molecular omics—can overcome the diagnostic challenges of Sjögren's disease, which often faces delays of 3-7 years due to heterogeneous symptoms and reliance on invasive biopsies. The authors systematically synthesize evidence that deep learning methods enable multimodal early detection, shifting from subjective assessment to data-driven diagnosis.

papers.title: Predicting Strain-Specific Metabolic Capabilities in the Genus Pseudomonas with a Flux-to-AI Approach Reveals Hidden Cell Envelope Properties.
papers.abstract: Bacteria from the Pseudomonas genus are omnipresent in air, soil, and water. They have been widely studied for their broad metabolic versatility and their presence in epidemiological chains, bioproduction, bioremediation, and disease processes. Each year, more genomic sequences are reported in databases and repositories. However, the relationship between genomic variability in Pseudomonas strains and the diversity of their metabolic capabilities across environmentally relevant phenotypes remains unknown. Additionally, predictive tools for analyzing different strains within a systematic framewo
papers.summary: This study presents a flux-to-AI approach that predicts strain-specific metabolic capabilities in Pseudomonas by linking genomic variability to metabolic phenotypes, revealing hidden cell envelope properties. The method offers a systematic framework for analyzing diverse Pseudomonas strains, which could aid in understanding their roles in bioproduction, bioremediation, and disease.

papers.title: An efficient ranking deep neural network algorithm for the prediction of Ca2+ binding sites of the protein.
papers.abstract: The Ca2+ binding sites of proteins are critical for their function, particularly in processes such as signal transduction, enzyme regulation, and structural stability. In this study, the calcium-binding sites of NtEhCaBP1 (Entamoeba histolytica calcium-binding protein). This paper proposes Statistical Ranking Deep Learning (SR-ML) to estimate the binding affinities of ten protein variants, The proposed SR-ML model computes the features in the proteins with the detection of sequences in the bindings. The classification of binding sites evaluated with the optimization of the features. With each
papers.summary: This paper introduces a deep learning-based ranking algorithm (SR-ML) to predict Ca2+ binding sites in proteins, applied to variants of the Entamoeba histolytica calcium-binding protein NtEhCaBP1. The model improves binding affinity estimation and site classification by optimizing feature detection, offering a potentially efficient tool for studying calcium-dependent protein functions.

papers.title: Generative AI-augmented transcriptomic and microbiome analysis across inflammatory and fibrotic disease states in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease (CD), a subtype of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) driven by chronic inflammation and resulting in irreversible structural damage requiring surgery. However, the molecular differences between inflammatory and fibrotic CD remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses generative AI to analyze transcriptomic and microbiome data from Crohn's disease patients, aiming to distinguish between inflammatory and fibrotic disease states. The findings help clarify molecular differences that could improve diagnosis and treatment of intestinal fibrosis.

papers.title: Representations of facial features and surface quality in monkey area TE compared to neural network models.
papers.abstract: The shape and spacing of facial features are essential for the perception of emotional expressions and the identification of individuals. The surface quality of faces, such as skin texture, eye twinkle, and hair gloss, is valuable for estimating health status. A previous fMRI study in monkeys revealed that regions selective for faces overlapped regions selective for object gloss in the central inferior temporal (IT) cortex, suggesting that the surface quality of faces is processed in area TE. However, the representation of facial surface quality has not been directly examined in this area. To
papers.summary: This study investigates how monkey area TE represents facial features and surface quality, comparing these representations to neural network models. The findings suggest that area TE encodes both facial shape and surface properties, with neural network models providing a useful framework for understanding these representations.

papers.title: A generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated XAI governance for cancer diagnostics: from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnostics is being reshaped by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, yet a persistent gap separates computational performance from clinical trust. Systematic reviews confirm that 83% of XAI studies in oncology excluded clinicians from development or evaluation, 87% lacked rigorous assessment of XAI explanations, and no universally accepted quality metrics for XAI outputs currently exist. Concurrently, generative AI (GenAI) is entering oncology at an unprecedented pace, yet it operates largely without formal interpretability governance.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated explainable AI (XAI) governance for cancer diagnostics, aiming to bridge the gap between computational performance and clinical trust. The framework combines multi-omics interpretation with lifestyle risk stratification, addressing the lack of clinician involvement and standardized quality metrics in current XAI approaches.

papers.title: DFN-kcr: a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation sites in human non-histone proteins.
papers.abstract: Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is extensively present in human non-histone proteins and plays a critical regulatory role in essential biological processes, including cell signaling and metabolic regulation. However, conventional wet-lab approaches for Kcr site identification are costly, time-consuming, and ill-suited for large-scale profiling. Although computational prediction methods have garnered increasing attention in recent years, there remains a notable lack of efficient and specialized tools tailored specifically for Kcr site prediction in human non-histone proteins.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces DFN-kcr, a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation (Kcr) sites in human non-histone proteins. The model addresses the lack of specialized computational tools for this task, offering a more efficient alternative to costly and time-consuming experimental methods.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in peptide cancer vaccine design: from neoantigen discovery to immunogenicity prediction.
papers.abstract: Peptide-based cancer vaccines represent a promising immunotherapeutic strategy aimed at inducing tumor-specific immune responses through the targeting of tumor-associated antigens and neoantigens. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing and immunogenomics have accelerated the identification of candidate neoantigens; however, the development of effective peptide vaccines remains limited by challenges related to antigen selection, HLA polymorphism, antigen processing, and variability in immunogenicity. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning approaches, h
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep learning, is being applied to improve peptide-based cancer vaccine design, from neoantigen discovery to immunogenicity prediction. It highlights AI's potential to address key challenges such as antigen selection, HLA polymorphism, and variability in immune responses, while noting current limitations in the field.

papers.title: Instability of LLM text embeddings for unsupervised dimension reduction of tabular data.
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) text embeddings have recently been used for supervised learning on tabular data by serializing each observation into text and then converting the text into a dense fixed-length vector. This strategy is appealing for biomedical tabular data, which are often mixed-type and contain missing values, because it produces a complete numeric representation even when some original entries are missing. However, its suitability for unsupervised tasks remains unclear. Here we evaluate the use of LLM-derived text embeddings for dimension reduction of tabular data, focusing on biol
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of LLM text embeddings for unsupervised dimension reduction of tabular biomedical data, finding that these embeddings are unstable for such tasks. The instability likely arises from the inherent variability in text serialization and embedding generation, which undermines reliable low-dimensional representations. The authors caution against using LLM embeddings for unsupervised analysis without further methodological refinements.

papers.title: Clinical AI-assisted FXR prioritization and WADDAICA-guided design of a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH: integrated computational and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), lack effective targeted therapies despite increasing global prevalence. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a key regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis, making it a promising therapeutic target. However, existing FXR modulators are associated with limited efficacy and adverse effects.
papers.summary: This study uses clinical AI-assisted prioritization of the FXR target and a computational design approach (WADDAICA) to develop a berberine-inspired analogue for treating MASH. The compound was validated experimentally, suggesting a potential new therapeutic strategy for this liver disease.

papers.title: Pooling multimodal cancer data across unaligned embedding spaces maintains tumor of origin signal.
papers.abstract: AI-based embeddings offer the possibilities of encoding complex biological data into low-dimensional spaces, called embedding spaces, that maintain the relationships between entities. Vector pooling is the process of aggregating an array of embedded vectors, either usually by summing or averaging, to summarize the total movement with the embedding space. Embedded vector pooling allows sampling of an arbitrary number of points to be summarized into a fixed sized vector, and is frequently used to sample networks of embedded values or to summarize protein language model vectors. There is an open
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether pooling embeddings from different AI models trained on different cancer data modalities can be combined while preserving the signal of tumor origin. The authors find that pooling across unaligned embedding spaces maintains tumor-of-origin information, suggesting a practical approach for integrating multimodal cancer data without requiring complex alignment.
